t: You're looking at Peckham Rye, a big open space in the London Borough of Southwark, just south of Peckham. It's roughly triangular and made of two parts that run into each other: Peckham Rye Common to the north and Peckham Rye Park to the south, with the road running around the western and eastern edges. A few notable people were born here. Elizabeth Cadbury, the philanthropist and activist who married the chocolate maker George Cadbury, started life here. So did the cricketer Charles Burls, and Robert Pearsall, who went on to design fire stations for the London Fire Brigade.
